Maria (PM): Quick sync — we need to pick the ordering for the Optimize toolkit work (quantization, batching, caching). Customers are pushing for cost wins fast. I propose we score ideas with RICE and set launch criteria: >=15% avg cost reduction on our two representative workloads (chat + embeddings), <=5% quality regression on dev evals, and no >10% increase in p95 latency. Thoughts?

Jared (Eng): +1 to RICE. Quick gut: quantization = biggest unit-cost win but highest engineering + QA cost. Batching = low infra effort, big throughput win but risk to p95 if naive. Caching = targeted wins for chat prefix reuse, very low risk.

Priya (ML): Quantization is high impact for large models, but model-specific edge cases (activation scaling, layernorm) mean we need eval harness and regen prompts. We should gate quantization rollouts behind objective eval pass/fail.

Sam (EngInfra): From infra side, we can ship dynamic batching with a deadline-based scheduler in ~2 weeks as a prototype. That lets us keep latency SLOs while getting throughput gains. That seems lower-risk than wholesale quantization first.

Ava (Customer Success): FYI — two pilot customers asked specifically for lower cost via quantization (willing to accept small quality tradeoffs). They care more about steady cost reductions than micro-p95 changes.

Jared (Eng): Quick RICE sketch (numbers are fuzzy):
```
Reach Impact Confidence Effort -> R*I*C/E
Quantization: 8 * 7 * 6 / 5 = 67.2
Batching (dynamic): 6 * 6 * 7 / 3 = 84
Caching (prefix KV): 4 * 5 * 8 / 2 = 80
```
So batching/caching look like faster wins per RICE math. Quantization still high total impact but higher effort/risk.

Priya (ML): Those confidence scores matter — quantization confidence should be lower until we run model-level evals. Suggest we add an extra column for "eval risk" in the spreadsheet.

Maria (PM): Proposal: do a two-track sequence to balance risk and customer asks:
1) Sprint 1: dynamic batching prototype (deadline scheduler) + small caching for hot prefixes (low-effort KV caching) — measurable wins, can ship fast.
2) Parallel POC: quantization experiments on 2 high-value models with strict eval gating; if POC passes, schedule rollout in Sprint 3 with canary + fallback.
Set launch criteria per feature: batching & caching must show >=10% cost per-request improvement and no p95 regression >8%. Quantization needs >=20% cost for heavy workloads and <5% quality degradation on evals to be considered for GA.

Sam (EngInfra): Agree. For batching, I want to prototype an adaptive deadline: bundle up to N tokens or wait up to T ms. We can tune T per model route. Defaults: N=64, T=25ms.

Jared (Eng): Sounds good. Action items: I'll spike the dynamic batching code this week, PR a prototype to the runtime repo.

Priya (ML): I'll run quant evals against our standard prompt suite for the two customer-requested models and produce a regression report next Wed. If patterns show >=5% generation drift, we stop.

Ava (Customer Success): I'll coordinate with the two pilot customers to get acceptance criteria and agree to be in the canary cohort for quantization POC.

Maria (PM): I'll populate the RICE sheet with the numbers above and formalize the launch criteria + guarded rollout plan. Plan to review in the next product sync.

release-bot: Created ticket OPT-1123: prototype dynamic batching (assignee: Jared).

Jared (Eng): Quick note — caching needs an evaluation harness too, otherwise we might over-cache and waste memory. I'll add a short metric for hit-rate and cost-per-token from cache.

Maria (PM): Nice. Ok team — consensus? If nobody objects by EOD I'll spin this up as the sprint plan. :thumbsup:

Sam (EngInfra): +1

Priya (ML): +1

Ava (Customer Success): +1; I'll send customer expectations doc to the thread.

Jared (Eng): +1; starting the spike now.
